newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Thursday were light at $64.00 per cwt, steady with late sales on Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
The bids generally were passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00, they said.
About 25,000 head sold late Wednesday in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, although numbers were seen higher once sales were finally counted, they said.
In Kansas, about 15,000 to 20,000 sold, but actual sales were probably larger, sources there said.
Outlooks for $65.00 cattle faded amid talk that beef prices were near a top following steep advances this week, several feedlot sources said.

"I think that beef has done its thing, and I think that's what the packer must feel, too, otherwise he'd jumping over himself trying to get cattle bought at $65.00," a Texas Panhandle feedlot manager said.
Choice beef weighing 700/850 lbs Wednesday was quoted at $103.73, up $1.26 from Tuesday, but up $5.61 since Friday, USDA statistics showed.
There were 304 fabricated beef loads sold on Wednesday. The week to date figure was 665, compared with 1,020 last week, the statistics showed.
